Hirsch.larman_bound.formal_statement:
namespace Hirsch

theorem larman_bound (d n : ℕ)
    (a : Fin n → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) (b : Fin n → ℝ)
    (hne : (Hpoly a b).Nonempty) (hbd : Bornology.IsBounded (Hpoly a b)) :
    DiamLE (Hpoly a b) (n * 2 ^ (d - 3)) := by sorry

end Hirsch
Hirsch.larman_bound.natural_language_statement: (Larman 1970.) Every nonempty bounded H-polytope in $\mathbb{R}^d$ described by $n$ inequalities has combinatorial diameter at most $n \cdot 2^{d-3}$. The bound is linear in the number of inequalities for each fixed dimension — still the best known bound of that shape. The exponent $d - 3$ is truncated natural subtraction, so for $d \le 3$ the asserted bound is $n$, which holds; lower-dimensional polytopes are included.
Hirsch.larman_bound.source: Larman, Paths on polytopes, Proc. London Math. Soc. s3-20 (1970) 161-178, https://doi.org/10.1112/plms/s3-20.2.249

Hirsch.hpoly_diameter_le_excess_of_rows_.theorem_title: Hirsch bound for H-polyhedra with at most three excess rows
Hirsch.hpoly_diameter_le_excess_of_rows_.formal_statement:
namespace Hirsch
theorem hpoly_diameter_le_excess_of_rows_le_dim_add_three
    (d n : ℕ)
    (a : Fin n → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) (b : Fin n → ℝ)
    (hrows : n ≤ d + 3) (hbd : Bornology.IsBounded (Hpoly a b)) :
    DiamLE (Hpoly a b) (n - d) := by sorry
end Hirsch
Hirsch.hpoly_diameter_le_excess_of_rows_.natural_language_statement: Let P be a bounded H-polyhedron in ambient R^d described by n real linear inequalities. If n is at most d+3, then its padded vertex-edge graph diameter is at most n-d (natural subtraction). The description may have redundant inequalities or zero normals, and P may be empty or lower dimensional. No strict feasibility or irredundancy is assumed. In particular, at most two excess describing rows gives diameter at most two. This is the classical small-excess consequence of low-dimensional Hirsch, not a uniform polynomial bound for arbitrary excess.
